items.title: Internal Symmetry-Driven Modal Convergence Enhances Chiral Scattering
authors: JaeWoo Park, Shuai Feng, Deeksha Satyabola, Abhishek Saji Kumar, Blake Povilus, Hao Yan, and Sui Yang
items.summary: Abstract Chiral scattering in nanostructures emerges from interference between electric and magnetic modes, yet its associated modal strength, arrangements and spectral concentration cannot be inferred from structural handedness alone. Using plasmonic nanorod dimers as a model system, we combine full-field electromagnetic simulations and single-particle circular differential scattering (CDS) spectroscopy to reveal how rotational and translational reconfigurations reshape modal overlap, coupling, and spectral organization even within an established handed architecture. We show that rotational asymmetry tunes the balance between electric-dipole (ED)- and magnetic-dipole (MD)-dominant chiral modes, while translational asymmetry controls their spectral separation and convergence. Consequently, the center-edge configuration produces enhanced and spectrally concentrated CDS responses coinciding with reduced chiral mode splitting and strengthened ED–MD coupling, a mode convergence regime supported both theoretically and experimentally. These results establish modal convergence as a design criterion for tailoring mode organization and scattering through internal symmetry in chiral nanophotonic systems.

items.title: Bimodal Pore Engineering of Mesoporous Carbon onto Ti 3 C 2 T x via a Soft–Hard Templating Route for Highly Durable Potassium-Ion Batteries
authors: Fengting Lv, Haitao Li, Cheng Tang, Aijun Du, Minghong Wu, and Haijiao Zhang
items.summary: Abstract Two-dimensional mesoporous carbon materials with tailored porosity and robust interfacial coupling are pivotal for potassium-ion batteries, yet the precise construction of bimodal pores remains a critical bottleneck. Herein, we propose an interfacial assembly strategy for the in situ growth of N,P-co-doped bimodal mesoporous carbon onto Ti 3 C 2 T x MXene (D-NMC/Ti 3 C 2 T x ) via a phytic acid (PA)-mediated soft–hard dual-templating route. Both theoretical and experimental results demonstrate that PA serves as a molecular bridge, reinforcing hydrogen-bonding interactions to orchestrate the coassembly of P123, SiO 2 nanospheres, and 2,6-diaminopyridine onto the functionalized Ti 3 C 2 T x surface. Attributed to the unique design, D-NMC/Ti 3 C 2 T x delivers a high reversible capacity of 303.6 mAh g –1 at 0.1 A g –1 over 200 cycles and retains 148.3 mAh g –1 after 3500 cycles at 1.0 A g –1 . XPS depth profiling reveals that the enhanced performance originates from a stable inorganic-rich solid electrolyte interphase that maintains electrode integrity. This work offers a promising strategy for designing advanced carbon-based electrodes.

items.title: Photoluminescence as a Quantitative Probe of Semiconductor Nanocrystals
authors: Leo Luber, Luca Reim, Daphne Benedikt, Andreas Singldinger, and Alexander S. Urban
items.summary: Abstract Photoluminescence spectroscopy is among the most established characterization techniques for semiconductor nanocrystals, yet routine analysis is often limited to the emission peak position and full width at half-maximum. Here, we identify a common statistical structure in ensemble photoluminescence and introduce a Gaussian asymmetric Laplace (GaLa) framework that transforms this structure into quantitative information about the emissive ensemble. The model describes emission as the convolution of a Gaussian contribution with independent low- and high-energy spectral tails. Temperature-dependent measurements reveal distinct thermal evolution of these contributions, while the same statistical form captures diverse nanocrystal compositions, morphologies, and environments. Where an appropriate size–energy relationship is available, the Gaussian width can be mapped onto relative size dispersion, while systematic deviations expose hidden emissive subpopulations. Applied during CsPbBr 3 nanocube syntheses, GaLa analysis simultaneously tracks nanocrystal growth and ensemble focusing, establishing routine photoluminescence as a quantitative probe of nanocrystal ensembles.

items.title: Accelerated Oxygen Redox Kinetics via Synergistic Electron Modulation at Asymmetric Dual 180° Oxygen Bonds in Co-Free Li-Rich Cathodes
authors: Yan Liu, Zewen Liu, Zhen Wu, Meiqi Wang, Jiadong Liang, Peifan Qu, Jilu Zhang, Qin Wang, Guopan Ren, Yide Qiao, Yuanzhen Chen, Qiang Tan, Yanli Nan, and Weibo Hua
items.summary: Abstract While oxygen redox in Li-rich cathodes enables exceptionally high capacities, its sluggish kinetics often lead to poor rate capability and severe voltage decay. Here, we construct asymmetric, near-180° Li–O–Al and Li–O–Na configurations that target the oxygen states in a Co-free, Mn-rich cathode. We demonstrate that Li–O–Al configuration lowers the energy barrier for oxygen electron excitation through strong Al–O covalency, whereas the Li–O–Na structure enhances the electron-loss capability of active oxygen. The interplay between these two configurations improves the kinetics of the oxygen redox reaction. This modulation effectively accelerates both electronic and ionic transport in lithium-rich materials during high-voltage cycling. The Al/Na codoped cathode delivers 314.8 mAh g –1 at 0.1 C and 151.2 mAh g –1 at 5 C, compared with 222.6 and 85.8 mAh g –1 for the undoped cathode. This dual-configuration strategy enables high-capacity and accelerated oxygen redox in Mn-rich, Co-free, and Li-rich cathodes.

items.title: Dark Exciton Signatures in the Infrared Transient Absorption of MoS 2 Monolayer
authors: Tian-Xiang Qian, Marco D’Alessandro, Claudio Attaccalite, Tian-Yi Cai, Sheng Ju, and Davide Sangalli
items.summary: Abstract Dark excitons play a central role in the nonequilibrium dynamics of two-dimensional semiconductors but remain difficult to characterize. Interexciton transient absorption (exc-tr-abs) in experiments, with probes tuned in the exciton–exciton transitions energy range, can detect excitations from any populated dark excitons, including symmetry-forbidden, spin-forbidden, and finite-momentum ones. In this work, we develop a GW +BSE scheme for computing exc-tr-abs spectra from arbitrary populated exciton distributions. These dark excitons are included equally by evaluating exciton–exciton dipoles in a locally smooth gauge, including intra- and interband contributions. For monolayer MoS 2 , the exc-tr-abs signal arises from the Γ, K, M, and Q valleys, differing substantially from the Γ-only interpretation. Exciton–exciton dipoles show similar intensities across these valleys, while their weights are dictated by initial excitonic populations. State- and spin-resolved analyses assign the peaks to 1s → 2p and 1s → 3p transitions from both spin-flip and spin-conserving A and B excitons across valleys and momenta.

items.title: In Situ Growth of Polyanionic DNA Hydrogel Networks for Nanoconfined Iontronic Analysis of DNA Methylation
authors: Bingheng Li, Zimeng Zhang, Yalei Gao, Bing Bo, Jian Ni, Liu Shi, and Liang Mao
items.summary: Abstract Solid-state nanofluidics offers unique ion transport dynamics for sensitive molecular diagnostics. Herein, we report a nanoconfined iontronic platform for quantifying trace p16 gene methylation ( p16 -mC) in liquid biopsies. This system couples sequence-specific hybridization with Hpa II enzymatic cleavage to strictly eliminate false positives from unmethylated homologues. Genuine target recognition triggers interfacial rolling circle and multiple-primer chain amplifications directly at anodic aluminum oxide nanochannel orifices. This in situ topological growth yields a 3D polyanionic DNA hydrogel that fundamentally remodels the interfacial physicochemical microenvironment. The resulting superhydrophilic transition and localized surface charge accumulation synergistically amplify transmembrane cation conductance, translating subtle epigenetic variations into robust iontronic readouts. Driven by this physical gating, the sensor achieves an ultralow detection limit of ∼33 aM and a dynamic range spanning 10 orders of magnitude. Clinically, the platform effectively discriminates nonsmall cell lung cancer patients from healthy donors using peripheral plasma, demonstrating its clinical feasibility for noninvasive cancer diagnostics.

items.summary: Abstract Interphase chemistry is conventionally ascribed to electrolyte composition, while electrochemical operating conditions are treated merely as kinetic parameters. Here, we demonstrate applied current programs at the solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) on Zn via an electrochemical kinetic-gating mechanism. N -Hydroxyethyliminodiacetic acid reorganizes Zn 2+ solvation and supplies interfacial precursors, whereas current density selects their reaction pathways. High-current activation enables stable Zn deposition even after switching to low current, evidencing that interphase properties are determined by formation history. The programmed anode delivers 5300 h at 5 mA cm –2 , and Zn||NH 4 V 4 O 10 pouch cells sustain 700 cycles. These findings establish current as an active control variable for interfacial reaction selection, offering a route toward programmable interphase chemistry beyond composition-only design.

items.title: Raman-Inactive Metal–Organic Framework Nanoribbons as Plasmonic-Nanocavity Spacers and Molecular Trappers for SERS Detection
authors: Yi Liu, Ruiqian Zhang, Shengyan Wang, Guoliang Zhou, Shuyu Zhu, Runfang Fu, Xiaolu Zhuo, and Jianfang Wang
items.summary: Abstract The integration of plasmonic nanostructures with metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) has emerged as a powerful strategy to enhance the sensitivity and selectivity of surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy (SERS). While the resultant hybrid systems exploit localized surface plasmon resonance for electric-field enhancement and MOF porosity for molecular enrichment, their practical applications are hindered by challenges, including intrinsic Raman interference from MOFs, precise control over MOF dimensions, and restricted plasmon coupling configurations. Herein we present a promising design featuring Raman-inactive MOF nanoribbons embedded within plasmonic nanogaps between a gold film and gold nanospheres (NSs). The sub-10 nm MOF interlayer eliminates Raman background while maximizing electromagnetic enhancement. The resultant Au-film/MOF/NSs architecture enables remarkable SERS performances with enhancement factors of 10 10 across diverse molecular sizes. This work not only enriches the toolbox of MOF-based plasmonic sensing platforms, but also opens the way for further exploration into other Raman-inactive MOFs and mechanisms.

items.title: Regulating the Spin-State and Frontier Orbital of a Molecular FePc Catalyst by Interlayer Electronic Coupling for Enhanced ORR Activity
authors: Yan Tan, Lin Ding, Aoshuang Li, Xiu-Cai Jiang, Yuhao Xia, Yiwen Cheng, Zhong Shi, Yu-Zhong Zhang, and Chuanwei Cheng
items.summary: Abstract Development of efficient and durable catalysts for the oxygen reduction reaction is essential for the advancement of metal–air batteries and fuel cells, yet it remains a significant challenge. Here, we present an interlayer-coupling strategy to modulate iron phthalocyanine by adjacent carbon-supported cobalt species. The resulting FePc@CoNC demonstrates superior ORR activity, with a half-wave potential of 0.927 V and achieving a peak power density of 336 mW cm –2 alongside cycling stability exceeding 1527 cycles. Density functional theory analysis reveals that the adjacent Co single atoms and Co nanoparticles synergistically enhance the localization of Fe d z 2 electrons while suppressing spin polarization of Fe 3d orbitals. This electronic modulation optimizes adsorption energetics of key intermediates involved in the rate-determining step, thereby accelerating ORR kinetics. These results elucidate the significance of interlayer electronic coupling in axially tuning spin states and frontier orbitals of molecular Fe–N 4 centers, offering a general strategy for enhancing oxygen electrocatalysis through electronic structure engineering.

items.title: An active Lorentz gas: walking droplets in periodic media
authors: Aleksi Majaniemi, Esko Toivonen, Rahil N Valani, Rainer Klages and Esa Räsänen
items.summary: The Lorentz gas is a paradigmatic model in dynamical systems theory for understanding the origin of nonequilibrium transport in terms of microscopic deterministic chaos. In the periodic setting, a point particle scatters elastically off disks arranged on a two-dimensional lattice. Here we replace the disks by smooth potentials and the particle by the widely studied walking droplet, which propels itself on a vertically vibrating fluid. In the low-memory limit, this droplet reduces to a particle with nonlinear active friction. We call this system an active Lorentz gas. Using extensive numerical simulations, we analyse how dissipation generated by the active deterministic dynamics alters the phase-space structure of the corresponding conservative Lorentz gas. We find that islands of stability collapse into attracting and repelling sets. To characterize these structures, we introduce an energy-variance filtering method that distinguishes localized periodic, quasi-ballistic periodic, and chaotic trajectories, enabling the construction of bifurcation diagrams in a non-conservative setting. We identify parameter regimes exhibiting strong bifurcation cascades, anomalous diffusion, and significant phase-space contraction. Our results establish the active Lorentz gas as a rich framework for studying transport in dissipative dynamical systems and provide a bridge between active matter and classical models of chaotic transport, with potential implications for hydrodynamic quantum analogs in periodic media.

items.title: Low-power Charge-domain In-FeRAM Computing
items.summary: Abstract The growing energy demands of large-scale model training and scientific computing have inspired interest in low-power computing paradigms. In-memory computing (IMC) reduces data movement overheads, but resistive devices suffer from high static power and Joule-heating. Here, we introduce a charge-domain computing paradigm based on Hf 0.5 Zr 0.5 O 2 ferroelectric random-access memory (HZO FeRAM), in which computation is enabled by linear accumulation of charge associated with the anti-orientated ferroelectric polarization. We experimentally demonstrate this concept using a 16-kbit HZO FeRAM array, where key computational characteristics execute directly within this array, gradient calculations are performed with errors below 6×10 − 3 , and in-memory difference operations solve partial differential equations with 98% accuracy after only 21 iterations. Hybrid FeRAM-digital training of a single-layer neural network for letter recognition is also shown. Furthermore, a 1 μm 2 HZO ferroelectric capacitor exhibits a measured switching energy of only 1.66×10 − 12 J, implying the potential of HZO FeRAM for energy-efficient charge-domain computing.

items.title: Interconnectivity of climate change and air pollution: from origin to action
Generative diffusion model with inverse renormalization group flows
items.summary: Natural data contain structure across multiple length scales, yet exploiting these correlations for efficient generation remains challenging. Masuki and Ashida introduce a diffusion model that uses renormalization group theory to systematically design a coarse-to-fine generation process. Applications to protein structure prediction and image generation demonstrate improved sample quality or sampling speed over denoising diffusion probabilistic model baselines with the same network architectures, highlighting how physical principles can guide the design of efficient generative models.

items.title: Non-Abelian space-time lattice gauge fields and higher-order topological states in topolectrical circuits
authors: Wenhui Cao, Weixuan Zhang, Xiaoqi Zhou, Fengxiao Di, Long Qian, Xiangdong Zhang
items.summary: Non-Abelian gauge fields provide a powerful framework for exploring exotic topological states, yet their interplay with space-time symmetries remains largely unexplored. Cao et al. introduce the concept of non-Abelian space-time lattice gauge fields and experimentally realize them using space-time topolectrical circuits, revealing geometry-dependent higher-order topological states and unconventional topological phase transitions with indirect band crossings. This opens avenues for exploring non-Abelian topological physics beyond the limitations of static systems.

items.title: Testing the validity of density scaling in glass physical aging
authors: Vasiliki Maria Stavropoulou, Federico Caporaletti, Simone Napolitano, Daniele Cangialosi
items.summary: Density scaling successfully describes how temperature and packing jointly control molecular motion in equilibrium liquids, but whether it applies to glasses has remained open. Stavropoulou et al. simultaneously track molecular relaxation and densification during physical aging of a molecular glass and show that the two evolve in strict proportionality. The proportionality factor is predicted, without adjustable parameters, from equilibrium density scaling parameters, extending this framework to the nonequilibrium glassy state.

items.title: Hierarchical Ionic Programming of Stretchable Organic Electrochemical Transistors for Dual-Mode Sensing and Computing
authors: Benfei Xu, Yuzhe Gu, Xuan Zhu, Xiaotian Wang, Baoguang Liu, and Yang Li
items.summary: Abstract Organic electrochemical transistors (OECTs) are promising building blocks for flexible in-sensor computing, yet the conflicting ionic dynamic demands of high-fidelity sensing and nonvolatile memory remain challenging to reconcile within a unified hardware platform. Here, we report a hierarchical compositional programming strategy that addresses this trade-off across a standardized stretchable OECT architecture. Regulating 2,2,6,6-tetramethylpiperidine-1-oxyl (TEMPO)-oxidized cellulose nanofiber content in poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene) (PEDOT) tunes channel capacitance and mechanical compliance, while tailoring the supramolecular network in a deep eutectic solvent gel electrolyte dictates ion retention kinetics. This strategy establishes distinct operational regimes via tailored formulations: a rapidly reversible, low-hysteresis state for sensing and a persistent ion trapping state for neuromorphic computing. The sensing OECT enables real-time electrocardiogram acquisition with a 35.6 dB signal-to-noise ratio and 98.9% biometric identification accuracy across 15 subjects. The computing state supports temporal Morse code demodulation and Pavlovian associative learning, demonstrating application-adaptive stretchable bioelectronics.

items.title: Long-lived light-driven bimagnons at finite momentum in NiO
items.summary: Light can manipulate magnetic order and its excitations on ultrafast timescales, including through resonantly driven phonons. In antiferromagnets, light can also create correlated magnon pairs, or bimagnons. Unlike single magnons, whose damping has been measured and modeled in detail, little is known about the lifetime, interactions and decay of such correlated pairs: prior two-magnon measurements show broad linewidths or coherences that dephase within 200 fs. Here we pump the phonon-assisted two-magnon absorption of NiO with mid-infrared pulses, far below its bandgap, and probe the resulting magnetic dynamics at finite momentum with time-resolved resonant inelastic X-ray scattering (RIXS). Upon photoexcitation, the one-magnon linewidth and energy are essentially unchanged, indicating that the long-range magnetic order is preserved without the photocarrier-induced demagnetization characteristic of above-bandgap excitation. A pump-induced two-magnon signal appears on the energy-gain (anti-Stokes) side of the spectrum. Its spectral weight peaks 4 ps after the pump, well beyond our 0.5 ps time resolution, indicative of a delayed growth likely due to momentum redistribution of the light-induced magnon pairs across the Brillouin zone. This two-magnon signal decays with a time constant of $28\pm11$ ps, exceeding the previously reported two-magnon dephasing time by more than two orders of magnitude. These results establish long-lived light-driven bimagnon correlations beyond the one-magnon state, akin to the higher-order correlations measured in ultracold gases.

items.title: Discrete Time Crystals from Anti-Unitary Floquet Driving and Dynamical Freezing
items.summary: We show anti-unitary periodic drive paves a direct path for stabilizing a Discrete Time-Crystal by Dynamical Freezing (DF). The magnetization appears as an emergent conserved operator, and an exact pairing of two-cycle quasi-energies pins the subharmonic response. DF keeps the effective Hamiltonian $\textit{quasi-local}$; infinite-chain simulations show no detectable decay for a generic state with any finite magnetization. We outline an experimental realization of the anti-unitary drive.

items.title: Ensemble phase transitions in measurement-unitary hybrid quantum circuits
items.summary: The universal properties of state ensembles generated by quantum dynamics provide a refined lens into Hilbert-space ergodicity and deep thermalisation, or lack thereof. We investigate deep-ergodicity breaking transitions of an ancillary qubit entangled with a system undergoing dynamics via hybrid quantum circuits, where unitary evolution is interspersed with projective measurements. Specifically, we analyse the statistical properties of two distinct state ensembles: the trajectory ensemble (TE) conditioned on the measurement outcomes of the hybrid circuit, and the projected ensemble (PE) generated by further projective measurements of the system at the final temporal boundary. We find that both ensembles undergo non-analytic changes -- ensemble phase transitions -- at the critical point of the measurement-induced purification transition, despite their first moments remaining completely maximally mixed and blind to the transition. For Haar-random circuits, the TE transitions from a trivial identity ensemble to the uniform Haar ensemble, while the PE transitions from the Haar ensemble to a trivial singleton pure state. In Clifford circuits, absence of non-stabiliserness limits the PE to a $1$-design, while the TE forms a $k$-design for $k \leq 3$. We demonstrate that these genuine ensemble transitions offer a clear physical mechanism for the measurement-induced entanglement or purification transitions, illustrating how the capacity to ergodically steer a quantum subsystem shifts from the temporal boundary measurements in the mixed phase to the bulk trajectory measurements in the pure phase.

items.title: Thermalization Across Scales on a Digital Quantum Processor
items.summary: Thermalization of isolated quantum many-body systems normally unfolds via dynamical spreading of entanglement across progressively increasing spatial scales. The speed of this dynamical process, however, can be affected by the presence of local disorder. Here we study the crossover between slow and fast thermalization in a disordered two-dimensional Heisenberg Floquet model using digital quantum simulations with up to 100 superconducting qubits. Our experiment measures subsystem purities and $Z$-basis marginal collision entropies for patches of up to $3\times 3$ qubits. We resolve the onset of thermalization across scales by tracking each quantity's approach to its asymptotic value. In regimes where the system is moderately entangled, we validate our calibrated quantum simulations against state-of-the-art classical simulations. Near the crossover to fast thermalization, the classical methods no longer reliably converge due to volume-law growth of entanglement. By exploring this computationally hard regime, our work establishes a frontier of applications for digital quantum computers in probing complex many-body thermalization.By exploring this computationally hard regime, our work establishes a frontier of applications for digital quantum computers in probing complex many-body thermalization.

items.title: Quantum Metrology and Quantum Battery in a Hyperfine-Coupled Spin System
items.summary: We investigate multiparameter quantum metrology and the energetic properties of an effective electron--proton spin system inspired by the hyperfine structure of the hydrogen atom. Considering the external magnetic field $\mathcal B$ and the hyperfine coupling strength $Λ$ as unknown parameters, we derive the quantum Fisher information matrix and establish the corresponding quantum Cramér--Rao bounds for their simultaneous estimation. We analyze the estimation precision and the correlations between the two parameters, showing that the weak-commutativity condition is satisfied despite the noncommutativity of the associated symmetric logarithmic derivatives. Independently, we explore the energetic properties of the system under a unitary charging protocol, characterizing its ergotropy, anti-ergotropy, storage capacity, and energy-basis coherence. We investigate the dependence of these quantities on the magnetic field, hyperfine coupling, temperature, and charging time. Our results provide a comprehensive characterization of the metrological properties and energetic performance of a hyperfine spin-based quantum system, highlighting its potential as a platform for quantum sensing and energy storage.

items.title: Statistics of Fock-space correlation lengths in the many-body localised phase
items.summary: The presence of long-ranged, many-body resonances in the many-body localised phase of disordered quantum systems is manifest in strong inhomogeneities of eigenstate amplitudes on the Fock space. We develop a quantitative, microscopic theory for this, centred on two-point Fock-space correlation functions. Exact diagonalisation of the disordered tilted-field Ising chain uncovers a stark contrast: typical correlations decay perfectly exponentially, whereas average correlations exhibit subexponential decay with systematic system-size dependence driven by rare resonant nodes. We show that this behaviour stems from an underlying distribution of Fock-space correlation lengths with a variance that scales inversely with system size. Crucially, the interplay of this distribution with the high-dimensional geometry of the hypercubic Fock-space graph, leads to the qualitative difference between the typical and average behaviours. The theory also allows us to derive the singularity spectrum of the many-body localised eigenstates, and to establish theoretically the anomalous symmetry violation of quantum multifractality as an inherent consequence of the Fock-space geometry.

items.title: SiC-BN composites with extreme thermal and environmental stability
items.summary: Ceramic materials that maintain structural integrity and resist thermal-shock under extreme conditions are critical for many applications. Here we show that spark plasma sintered composites containing equal weight fractions of hexagonal silicon carbide (6H-SiC) and boron nitride (h-BN) exhibit exceptional stability under extreme high-temperature oxidizing conditions and unusually stable temperature-independent thermal conductivity across a broad temperature range. Under high-velocity oxygen-fuel torch exposure in air, it withstands prolonged heating and thermal-cycling at surface temperatures reaching >1500 °C, whereas pure 6H-SiC and h-BN rapidly fractures or erodes. Microstructural evaluation shows the formation of a multi-phase surface silica layer that further protects the material from oxidation. Finite-element analysis heat-flux map shows that intrinsic porosity mitigates thermal stress, while ReaxFF molecular dynamics simulations reveal thermally driven interfacial reconstruction and the formation of a Si-N/C-B-rich bonding network, enhancing the interfacial cohesion at elevated temperatures. This lightweight, easily machinable ceramic composite will be a promising structural material in extreme environment applications.

items.title: Interactions from memory footprints: Cage-hopping, mnemotaxis & nonreciprocity
items.summary: Cellular motility is integral to biological processes ranging from foraging to immune responses and cancer metastasis. While cells often navigate by sensing pre-existing environmental cues, many actively steer their future trajectories by remodeling their surroundings via shared, long-lived physicochemical trails called memory footprints. These stigmergic responses to shared footprints also influence large-scale self-organization, such as the early stages of microcolony formation. Despite recent progress, a unified framework connecting single-cell dynamics and collective organization through effective pairwise interactions remains elusive. To bridge this gap, we perform extensive agent-based simulations of an interacting random walk model that explicitly accounts for footprint deposition and decay. Our approach reveals distinct cage-hopping dynamics in solitary cells, as well as complex mnemotactic responses to externally imposed memory gradients. Furthermore, we demonstrate that shared spatial memory fields generate nontrivial effective pairwise interactions, both reciprocal and nonreciprocal, that shape the collective organization of cell populations. Beyond multiscale cellular dynamics, our findings have broader implications for the collective behavior of synthetic active matter, such as swarm robots.

items.title: Inter-Nanoparticle Repulsion Effect on Self-Organization in Polymer Nanocomposites: A Langevin Dynamics Simulation Study
items.summary: Demixing through liquid-liquid phase separation is relevant to nanoparticle (NP) aggregation in polymer nanocomposites (PNCs), biomolecular compartmentalization, and liquids embedded in elastic networks. Mixing-demixing phase behavior depends on factors, such as particle size distribution, system dimen-sionality, intermolecular interactions, and relative concentrations. Here, using Langevin Dynamics simu-lations, we systematically investigate the effect of inter-nanoparticle repulsion on the self-assembly of PNCs under extreme confinement. A nanoparticle assembly, in the form of a compact droplet, is immersed in a polymer matrix of semiflexible, rod-like chains. By varying the nanoparticle-nanoparticle repulsion strength, while fixing all other interactions, we identify four distinct regimes with respect to the self-assembled NP morphologies: droplet, slab, crystalline droplet, and dispersed. Cluster-based analysis reveals a progressive loss of nanoparticle droplet integrity, leading to fragmentation within the dispersed regime. Local order of the nanoparticle assembly and global order of polymer chains are gauged through refined descriptors, quantifying the degrees of crystallinity and of nematic order, respectively. Interest-ingly, the slab regime exhibits negligible nanoparticle crystallization yet demonstrates the strongest polymer nematic ordering. In contrast, the crystalline droplet displays extensive triangular close-packed crystallites accompanied by a significant reduction in polymer nematic order, owing to its rhomboid shape. In the dispersed regime, nanoparticle fragmentation facilitates efficient mixing and local smectic-like ordering of the polymer chains. These findings demonstrate that fine-tuning inter-NP repulsions can control self-organization and the resulting morphologies, providing insights into PNCs with tailored functionality.

items.title: A stochastic heat engine driven using a nonlinear protocol
items.summary: A colloidal particle confined in a time-dependent optical trap can function as a microscopic heat engine, with optimization strategies offering a route to enhanced performance. Here, we numerically investigate a Stirling heat engine operating in passive and active environments using a protocol inspired by Engineered Swift Equilibration (ESE). We analyze various fluctuating parameters throughout the cycle to validate the robustness of the engine, and demonstrate a significant enhancement in performance compared to conventional Stirling engines. Most crucially, we observe that the nonlinear protocol can even transform a heat pump-like operation into a genuine heat engine under strong activity, thereby surpassing bounds imposed on efficiency by high-temperature and quasi-static conditions. In contrast to the standard Stirling protocol, we observe that the nonlinear protocols appear to suppress the finite-time relaxation lag of the system from reaching an instantaneous equilibrium distribution, thereby improving engine performance at short cycle times. An analytical analysis of the variance dynamics where we quantify the relaxation lag between the actual and instantaneous equilibrium states clearly vindicates our understanding about the improved efficacy of the non-linear protocols. The proposed protocol is designed with experimental feasibility in mind, providing a practical route toward efficient microscopic heat engines.

items.title: Circular phonons generate negligible magnetization in insulators
items.summary: The optical excitation of circular phonons has opened up non-equilibrium phenomena with no equilibrium counterparts, ranging from the generation of synthetic magnetic fields to the control of topological order or the manipulation of ferroaxial states. In this area, significant controversy has arisen on whether sizeable "true" magnetizations accompany circular phonons. Several confounding factors cloud the interpretation of the experiments, which are based on probing polarization rotation in the driven material. These range from the interpretation of the Faraday effect in non-equilibrium conditions to spurious nonlinear optical contributions in pump probe experiments. Here we resolve these ambiguities by measuring both polarization rotation inside the driven material and the stray magnetic field generated outside it with a proximate Faraday detector. For a 5 MV/cm mid-infrared drive, we observe a colossal polarization rotation inside a driven SiC crystal, similar to what was reported in previous work. Depending on the assumptions made, this could correspond to magnetizations as high as $μ_0 M = 0.3 T$ or as low as 4 $μT$. However, when measuring the magnetic stray field outside the driven sample we unambiguously determine that the magnetization in SiC is negligibly small ($μ_0 M \lt 0.001 T$).

items.title: Integer and Fractional Chern Plateaus Shaped by Layer-Dependent Disorder
items.summary: The realization of integer and fractional Chern insulators in moiré systems provides a lattice setting for exploring how the structure of Bloch wave functions influences the interplay between topology and disorder. Here we investigate how layer-dependent disorder shapes Hall plateau widths and transitions. Using a realistic three-orbital model of twisted bilayer MoTe$_2$, we compare Hall and bulk transport under onsite-potential, displacement-field, and twist-angle disorder. At equal bare disorder strength, onsite-potential disorder produces broad integer plateaus with nearly direct transitions, whereas displacement-field disorder yields narrow plateaus separated by conducting regions with pronounced Hall-resistance dips. These contrasting behaviors arise from the layer composition of the Bloch states: contributions from different layer under displacement-field disorder partially cancel, weakening the bulk localization. Composite-fermion mean-field theory further yields fractional plateaus at $ν_h=2/3$ and $3/5$ with the same disorder dependence of plateau widths. These findings identify layer-dependent disorder as an important mechanism shaping Chern plateau stability in moiré systems beyond bare disorder strength alone.

items.title: Physically Interpretable Basin Selection in Discrete-Variable Origami Design
items.summary: Automatic differentiation has enabled rapid progress on continuous-variable mechanical design problems, but gradient-based optimization still struggles with discrete variables. The standard approach is to optimize using a continuous relaxation of the choices, then commit to the nearest discrete design at the end. Why this procedure selects unfavorable basins is poorly understood. Here, we introduce a practical, interpretable design problem inspired by origami, in which automatic differentiation is used to design shapes with a target functional behavior. Each origami sheet has a fixed geometry, and a bilevel optimization framework tunes which one of four discrete hinge types to place at each fold. Baseline gradient-based design settles into basins with a large discretization gap: relaxed optimization solves 97% of runs, but the final, discrete solutions succeed only half the time. We find that the gap can be relieved with a surprisingly simple modification. An initialization prior uniformly biased toward the stiff, flat hinge option boosts the final solve fraction from 49% to 69%. Applying the prior adds no additional compute and leaves the optimization process unchanged. Compared to the baseline, sheets produced with the prior have greater geometric compatibility and mechanical stiffness. Directly penalizing frustration and floppiness in the outer loss function produces an even greater improvement than the prior does, raising the solve fraction to 78% and indicating that these properties help distinguish the unfavorable basins. Our results demonstrate that loss landscapes for mechanical design can have physically meaningful basins that are not robust to discretization and cause solves to fail. Targeting these basins' physical signatures, even with just an initialization bias, helps avoid them.

items.title: Cubic, Non-Fermi Liquid Exchange Couplings for Doublet Impurities
items.summary: We construct non-Fermi liquid (NFL) quantum impurity models for doublet impurities in a cubic metal, involving conduction electrons with half-integer total angular momentum, $J$. We highlight the only two crystal-symmetry-protected NFL quantum impurity models: the spin-half impurity, $J=3/2$ conduction electron Kondo model, and the two-channel Kondo model originally derived in the context of the quadrupolar Kondo model. We show explicitly that the quadrupolar Kondo model preserves time-reversal symmetry. We also construct two cubic quantum impurity models in which NFL behavior is not symmetry-protected. Each has $Γ_8$ and either $Γ_{6}$ or $Γ_{7}$ conduction electrons screening the impurity simultaneously, one model for a non-Kramers doublet and the other for a Kramers doublet impurity ground state. To our knowledge, the latter model has not been considered before; we expect it to realize a new NFL fixed point, but its solution is left for future work. Finally, we derive the relevant cubic perturbation that drives the non-symmetry-protected systems away from their NFL scaling regimes.

items.title: Optimizing Chern Bands for Moore-Read States: A Parent Hamiltonian Approach
items.summary: The recent realization of fractional quantum anomalous Hall states in moiré materials motivates efforts to stabilize non-Abelian topological order in the absence of a magnetic field. Here, we propose a framework for optimizing interactions to favor the non-Abelian Moore-Read state. Our approach compares band-projected three-particle spectra to that of the Moore-Read parent Hamiltonian, which is defined by a three-body interaction, and quantifies the comparison by defining a cost function that estimates proximity to the ideal Moore-Read limit. We apply our approach to Landau levels and to the Chern bands of twisted MoTe$_2$.

items.title: Lattice response theory for subsystem symmetry-protected topological phases
items.summary: We develop a framework to study subsystem symmetry-protected topological (SSPT) phases using lattice response theory. We begin with a systematic construction of spacetime lattice gauge fields from general microscopic $X$-type symmetry actions on qudit systems, including global symmetries, subsystem symmetries, and more general modulated symmetries. Given a gauge-invariant response action, we then construct a corresponding entangler and explicitly show that it implements stacking with the SSPT phase described by the response action. We show that a broad class of SSPT phases can be described by intersection pairings and realized by cluster entanglers. We also study SSPT phases beyond intersection pairings, including those described by subsystem analogues of type-II group cocycles involving the Bockstein homomorphism. We construct a new 3+1d SSPT phase protected by two 2-foliated planar subsystem symmetries and a global 0-form symmetry, whose response action is a subsystem analogue of a type-III cocycle. On its boundary, the 0-form symmetry acts by stacking with a 2+1d linear SSPT phase, signaling a mixed 't Hooft anomaly.

items.title: The de Haas--van Alphen effect in a two-dimensional nematic Fermi fluid
items.summary: Quantum oscillations are widely used to probe the Fermi surface of metals, but their behavior becomes more complex when electronic interactions can spontaneously deform that surface. We investigate this interplay in a two-dimensional model of interacting electrons capable of developing nematic order, using a uniform mean-field approximation in a perpendicular magnetic field. We show that Landau quantization can favor or suppress nematic order as the field varies, producing alternating isotropic and nematic regions near a Pomeranchuk instability, with both continuous and first-order transitions. Conversely, the evolving nematic order modifies the de Haas--van Alphen oscillations in ways that depend on the thermodynamic conditions. At fixed chemical potential, the oscillation frequency can change significantly even when the cyclotron mass varies only modestly. At fixed particle density, conservation of the Fermi-surface area preserves the leading Onsager frequency, while the cyclotron mass and harmonic amplitudes remain sensitive to nematic order. The magnetization and magnetic susceptibility provide additional signatures of the nematic transitions. These results show how quantum oscillations can both reveal and influence electronic order, offering a framework for interpreting experiments in strongly correlated metals.

items.title: A reason why we do not observe Schrödinger's cats
items.summary: A reason is discussed (may be not the only one) for why we do not see any superposition of macroscopic states in the real world. Under the general assumption that quantum macrostates are statistical ensembles of microstates, it is shown that any superposition of macrostates is reduced in a very short time by the unitary dynamics of the ordinary Schrödinger equation, deducing the Born rule without having to postulate it. In more detail, the macroscopic and microscopic degrees of freedom are decoupled in the Schrödinger equation, yielding an effective stochastic equation for the macroscopic variables, with the ensemble average of the microscopic amplitudes that acts as a self-generated internal white noise. The stochastic equation is shown to be a reducing Itô equation if some general causality conditions are met, predicting a very quick collapse of any macroscopic superposition upon formation, with probabilities which satisfy the Born rule. In the context of the von Neumann measurement scheme, the relevance of the result is discussed as a simple dynamical solution of the measurement problem.

items.title: Reentrant Nematicity from Landau Quantization near a Pomeranchuk Instability
items.summary: Landau quantization can induce nematic order in a two-dimensional Fermi liquid that is isotropic at zero magnetic field. Using a mean-field theory near a quadrupolar Pomeranchuk instability, we show that varying the magnetic field produces alternating nematic and isotropic regions, with transitions that can be either continuous or first order. The resulting nematic state also leaves distinctive signatures in the de Haas--van Alphen oscillations. At fixed chemical potential, the field-dependent deformation of the Fermi surface can produce substantial changes in the oscillation frequency, even when the cyclotron mass varies only modestly. At fixed particle density, conservation of the Fermi-surface area preserves the leading oscillation frequency, while the cyclotron mass and harmonic amplitudes remain sensitive to nematic order. These contrasting behaviors provide experimentally relevant signatures of field-induced nematicity and reveal the importance of thermodynamic constraints in quantum-oscillation measurements.

items.title: A neural quantum state variational Monte Carlo study of Aharonov-Casher bands
items.summary: We use neural-network-based variational Monte Carlo to investigate the competition between fractional Chern insulators and generalized Wigner crystals in the Aharonov-Casher Hamiltonian, a continuum model for moiré materials. We introduce a variational wave function inspired by flux attachment that captures fractionalized phases and, by comparing its energy with that of a Slater--Jastrow ansatz that captures crystalline phases, we determine the phase diagram at fractional fillings in regimes of strong band mixing and for system sizes beyond the reach of other methods. We find that discrete translation symmetry, encoded in a nonuniform quantum geometry, affects fractionalized states at filling fractions $ν=1/3$ and $ν=2/3$ differently, and that band mixing can stabilize incommensurate crystalline ground states. Our results further reveal the delicate competition between topological and non-topological crystalline phases.

items.title: A Reduced Order Model for First-Principles Atomistic Simulations
items.summary: To leverage the redundancy between the electronic structure computed for various model parameters such as varying atomic positions, we present a data-driven modeling framework for Kohn-Sham Density Functional Theory that bypasses the explicit optimization of electronic wavefunctions. We sample \textit{a priori} representative atomic configurations and construct a low-dimensional basis that efficiently approximates the electronic structure subspace. Subsequently, we employ this reduced basis in an iterative solver for the electronic single particle density matrix, thereby enabling the efficient determination of ground state without iterative wavefunction optimization. We demonstrate the accuracy of our approach in a Born-Oppenheimer molecular dynamics of a water molecule, showing that the resulting simulations accurately reproduce key structural properties, such as bond lengths and bond angle, obtained from full first-principles molecular dynamics. This work highlights the potential of data-driven approaches to develop low-dimensional electronic structure representations for first-principles simulations.

items.title: Exact characterization of three-terminal fermion counting under one-body scattering
items.summary: Quantum scattering is a fundamental probe of the scattering region and the quantum dynamics of outgoing particles. In two terminals, the statistics of non-interacting fermions is described by a generalized binomial distribution, that arises from the Pauli exclusion principle, while deviations are a signature of interactions. In this work, we extend this result to a scattering region coupled to three outgoing terminals (or channels), obtaining exact bounds for the statistics of the outgoing fermions. In particular, for two fermions and three terminals, four inequalities involving six measured probabilities determine whether a non-interacting scatterer can explain the observed statistics. Applying these inequalities to recent scattering experiments in cold atoms, we are able to identify a regime where interactions have a significant contribution on the outgoing particles. Therefore, our work opens up the possibility of identifying fermion interactions at the nanoscale in systems that range from mesoscopic conductors to optical traps in cold atoms.

items.title: Dissipative framework for subsystem dynamics of noninteracting quantum chains
items.summary: When only local observables of a many-body quantum system are of interest, it is desirable to formulate a reduced description within the Hilbert space of the corresponding subsystem, with the remaining degrees of freedom traced out and acting as an environment. Assuming initially uncorrelated states and Gaussian environments, we develop a framework for reconstructing the local dynamical generator of noninteracting quantum chains, with polynomial computational effort. As an application, we consider two representative models: a bipartitioned Kitaev chain and a Kitaev chain boundary-coupled to a fully connected free-fermion environment. In both models, strong subsystem-environment coupling leads to non-Markovian dynamics characterized by ballistic spreading of the Lindblad dissipator support within the subsystem. On the other hand, weak coupling to a fully connected environment yields predominantly boundary-localized, Markovian dissipation. Our work highlights the implications of subsystem-environment correlations on the generator of local dynamics, beyond the conventional weak-coupling approximations.

items.title: Acoustically driven motion of single molecules at hBN surfaces
items.summary: Developments in single-molecule imaging and sensing techniques have enabled direct observation of biomolecular dynamics at interfaces, which has important implications for the fields of membrane biophysics, nanofluidic sensing and transport. However, integrating active surface transport, localization and control over molecule motion remains challenging, limiting further progress in the realization of single-molecule devices. Here, we introduce an integrated surface acoustic wave (SAW)-hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) platform as a contactless actuation platform for directional transport of biomolecules over hBN surfaces. hBN provides an atomically flat surface on which DNA can be confined and still retain in-plane mobility, whereas SAW actuation enables active and guided transport without requiring specific electrical, dielectric or magnetic properties of the biomolecules. Trajectory- and jump-based analyses show that increasing the SAW power leads to higher displacement bias in the streaming direction, resulting in transport velocities along increasingly more linearized trajectories. We thus demonstrate that SAWs can induce tunable directional transport of DNA molecules confined on hBN surfaces, providing a new approach for the on-chip manipulation of biomolecules in nanofluidic systems. Our findings have important implications for the development of advanced single-molecule sequencing platforms and other technologies for biomolecular manipulation and analysis.

items.title: High-pressure behavior of the low-frequency mode of water
items.summary: The low-frequency (LF) mode observed in the THz spectrum of liquid water near 10 meV has been known for decades, yet its microscopic origin remains debated. Leading interpretations assign it to a transverse acoustic-like excitation, a transverse optic-like mode, or a mode-mode coupling mechanism. We address this question by probing the collective dynamics of H$_2$O and D$_2$O at room temperature and pressures from 0.1 to 1 GPa using high-resolution (1.6 meV) inelastic X-ray scattering (IXS). The LF mode remains heavily damped, close to critical damping, throughout the explored range, while its frequency hardens markedly with pressure, much more than expected for a transverse acoustic mode. Comparison with IXS measurements and \textit{ab initio} simulations of crystalline Ice VI reveals a cluster of weakly dispersive modes in the same energy range, suggesting that the low-frequency mode in liquid water reflects a mixed character arising from the superposition of several branches rather than a single well-defined excitation, providing a coherent microscopic picture of water's anomalous THz dynamics under compression.

items.title: Time reparametrization across kinetic rules in a glass-forming liquid
items.summary: Monte Carlo algorithms combining swap moves with kinetic constraints allow the relaxation pathways of a liquid to be modified without changing its equilibrium measure. Recent work suggests that much of this change can be absorbed into a time reparametrization, yielding a near-collapse of parametric relations between overlaps measured at different spatial scales. We examine this correspondence in a three-dimensional polydisperse hard-sphere liquid by comparing a planar $f_P$ rule that confines the translation of a fraction of particles to randomly oriented planes with a pure-$f_R$ rule that restricts swap participation. At each packing fraction, the two rules are tuned to comparable structural relaxation times, and time is eliminated explicitly. For $0.58 \leq φ\leq 0.62$, we find a near-collapse accompanied by a small but resolved residual that persists when directly confined particles are excluded from the observable. A self--distinct decomposition shows that the statistics of individual displacements reproduce most of the scale of this residual. Among translationally free particles, the probability of large displacements decreases as the relative directions to constrained neighbors become more aligned with their forbidden normals, even when the number of constrained neighbors is held fixed. This association is consistent with zero in a ghost control, where the same normals impose no translational restriction. Our findings complement the time-reparametrization picture by showing that a near-collapse of collective parametric relations can coexist with rule-dependent displacement statistics and an orientational signature in the mobility of particles that are not directly constrained.

items.title: How Does Incubation Affect Laser Material Processing?
items.summary: In the last decades, the subject of laser-induced damage (LID) moved from a topic of scientific interest toward laser material processing for technical applications. When using pulsed lasers, the cumulative effect known as incubation is one of the most fundamental features of the processing event. Incubation manifests by the fact that the critical fluence for LID (known as laser-induced damage threshold, LIDT) depends on the number of pulses N exciting one spot on the sample. In most cases, the threshold fluence decreases with N starting from the single-shot ablation threshold and remains constant for large N. No ablation or damage occurs for any N, if the fluence is kept below the multiple-pulse threshold. In contrast, examples where the LIDT increases with N have been reported. The latter effect is known as laser conditioning and is advantageously used when ramping up the power of high-power laser systems. Incubation has been described for many types of solids; the motivation for these comprehensive efforts is twofold. Firstly, one tries to prevent the damage of optical materials in the beam path of high-energy or high-peak-power lasers. Secondly, one deliberately uses this damage for the sculpting of components. In this chapter, we introduce the reader to the mechanisms of incubation. We are going to look at the parameters controlling LID and highlight the peculiarity of the parameter "number of pulses". We will give an overview of the experimental work done in a variety of materials. There are several physical and chemical mechanisms proposed that govern incubation, and there are several mathematical models to describe the behavior of threshold fluence and ablation rate in dependence on the number of pulses. In a few cases, the two classes of mechanisms are even related to each other. Eventually, we will show the implications that incubation has on real-world laser machining.

items.title: Theory of critical behavior at non-polar structural phase transitions from functional renormalization
items.summary: $O(N)$ models provide a versatile framework for describing continuous phase transitions in a wide variety of physical systems. We investigate an extension of these models arising from order parameters that transform under interlocked internal and spatial symmetries which describe transitions towards non-polar structural order. Such order occurs, for instance, in dipolar antiferromagnets, spin-orbit-coupled magnets, non-polar ferroics, and certain nematic systems. The resulting effective theory is an $O(d)$ model with an additional symmetry-allowed kinetic term $h(\partial_iφ_i)^2$, which modifies the relative stiffness of longitudinal and transverse fluctuations. We study both thermal and quantum phase transitions within this $O(d)$ model using the functional renormalization group (FRG). In contrast to conventional $O(N)$ models, the interlocking of internal and spatial symmetries distinguishes spatial and imaginary-time derivatives, such that the quantum model is not simply obtained from the thermal one by a dimensional extension $d\rightarrow d+1$. We derive and analyze the corresponding FRG flow equations, paying particular attention to the tensor structure of the two-point function, which is essential for consistently extracting the flow of the kinetic terms. Our analysis shows that the additional kinetic coupling is irrelevant at the $O(d)$ Wilson-Fisher fixed point in both thermal and quantum cases, where quantum-to-classical correspondence thus re-emerges. However, its small but sizable correction-to-scaling exponent gives rise to substantial corrections to scaling in the vicinity of the critical point.

items.title: Asymmetric Frequency Conversion and Violation of Kirchhoff's Law of Thermal Radiation in Phased Floquet Metasurfaces
items.summary: We study a system of three closely spaced conducting sheets, whose thermal emission largely violates Kirchhoff's law through nonreciprocal frequency conversion enabled by Floquet phenomena. We leverage surface mode transitions controlled by temporal modulation of one of the metasurfaces, resulting in largely asymmetric frequency conversion. Our findings broaden the capabilities of Floquet metasurfaces for wave conversion and energy manipulation, paving the way towards magnet-free nonreciprocal photonic devices with opportunities for thermal management and efficient photonic refrigeration.

items.title: Multi-particle quantum walk search on a two-dimensional lattice
items.summary: In the present paper we study the formulation of a search problem and the efficiency of multi-particle quantum walk search algorithms. The discrete-time evolution of each particle in space is treated according to Grover's quantum walk evolution operator. We focus on the local interactions models, where the particles' states are modified only when two or more of them appear on the same grid site. The main focus is given to the two-dimensional grid in space. We study the dependence of the search algorithm asymptotic success time and probability on the interaction strength and the generated maximal entanglement between particles. We show that the interacting and non-interacting two- and three-particle search algorithm attains a constant factor improvement over the single-particle counterpart. In addition, we provide a new generalized model of interactions for multi-particle quantum walks.

items.title: De Sitter Gravity and Emergent Time from Fusion Matrix Product States and SYK
items.summary: We propose a quantum-mechanical model dual to two-dimensional de Sitter (dS) gravity. It is a quantum channel, defined by a matrix product state that fuses one spin at each step, and is related to a limit of the Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev model without chord crossings. Its simplest part is a random walk with an emergent $SL(2,\mathbb R)$ symmetry, which we identify with the symmetry of the future boundary of dS. It selects a time variable in which the walk obeys the Schwarzian action and yields the disk amplitude of dS Jackiw-Teitelboim gravity. As the simplest case, we consider free massless scalar fields in the fixed background of dS$_2$. We find the agreement of the two-point function in the Bunch-Davies vacuum and the matching of symmetry. Our construction provides a concrete model for the dS/CFT correspondence for two-dimensional de Sitter gravity.

items.title: Ergodicity breaking for data classification in a dissipative Ising model with competing two- and four-body interactions
items.summary: We explore the close relationship between the processing of data and the dynamics of interacting many-body systems. For example, certain classes of quantum neural networks can be mapped onto dissipative quantum Ising models whose evolution is described by a Lindblad master equation. In these architectures, emergent nonlinearities lead to non-ergodic dynamics under which initial states located in different basins of attraction evolve towards distinguishable stationary states. This mechanism underlies the classification of quantum data. Motivated by this connection, we consider an Ising model with competing two- and four-body interactions. Using a combination of mean-field calculations and exact small-scale numerics, we show that the stationary state manifold can be designed to enable multi-class classification. We also investigate the structure of the ensuing basins of attraction, thereby showing that these systems allow for the classification of quantum states with nonlinear decision boundaries.

items.title: Sedimentation of flexible fibers through an ordered array of pillars
items.summary: In this study, we extend our previous work [Makanga \textit{et al.}, Physical Review Fluids 8, 044303 (2023)] to investigate the effects of a periodic array of pillars on the settling dynamics of a flexible fiber in a viscous fluid. By means of numerical simulations, we show that the fiber trajectory falls at long times into one of two migration modes, ``zigzag" and ``displacement", which are determined by the short-time scattering dynamics induced by fiber-pillar interactions. In the zigzag mode, there is no average displacement relative to the direction of gravity; the center of mass of the fiber follows a quasi-straight line. Conversely, in the displacement mode, there is a net displacement relative to the direction of gravity; the fiber center of mass follows a cyclical skew-bumping path. We show how this long-time behavior can be predicted using a theoretical model with minimal ingredients. These findings, together with the long-time transport properties of the fiber, provide insights into future experiments, as well as the design of gravity-based deterministic lateral displacement (DLD) devices to sort elongated particles based on their geometric and/or mechanical properties.

items.title: Reflection Zeros Set the Scattering Invariant of Finite Majorana Wires
items.summary: Majorana modes, zero-energy excitations of superconducting wires that are their own antiparticles, could store quantum information protected from local noise. In transport experiments, however, ordinary bound states mimic their signature, a conductance peak at zero voltage, and whether Majorana modes have been observed remains debated. A sign, $Q$, of the electron reflection at zero energy marks the topological phase of a long wire, but what $Q$ certifies in a finite device has been unclear. Here we show for the first time that $Q$ counts reflectionless states, waves that enter through one contact and leave entirely through the other: $Q=-1$ when an odd number of them lie in the lower half of the complex energy plane. In a finite wire this means that the two Majorana modes are split by less than their coupling to the contacts. With equal contacts, every sign change of $Q$, including the bulk topological transition, is an exceptional point at which two such states merge and transmission is maximally flat. At zero temperature, $Q=-1$ exactly when the zero-bias conductance measured at a contact exceeds $e^2/h$. These results show what transport can certify about a Majorana device and how to read the invariant from conductance.

items.title: Dynamical mean-field theory of latching Potts networks
items.summary: Spontaneous transitions between memories, as observed in internally generated cognition such as mind-wandering and free association, require neural dynamics capable of destabilizing one attractive memory state and moving towards another. We ask what minimal representational structure is required for such transitions to emerge in random associative networks. To address this question, we study Potts associative networks with $S$ active states per unit and slow adaptive thresholds. The $S=1$ case can model a standard Hopfield-like network of binary units. We employ dynamical mean-field theory in the extensive-load regime, where the number of stored patterns scales linearly with network size and connectivity, and we focus on transitions between two condensed memories, which are singled out in the connectivity matrix. In the finite-load regime, we show that transitions are governed by an effective drive term, whose sign and temporal evolution distinguish high-latching (structured), low-latching (random), and non-latching regimes. The resulting phase diagram shows that adaptation alone is not sufficient: transitions only occur within certain ranges of the overlap between the two memories. In the binary case $S=1$, in particular, no unit can be active in both memories but in different Potts states, thus strongly supressing the high-latching, structured transitions that exist for $S>1$. In the extensive-load regime, non-condensed memories generate colored fluctuations and retarded self-interactions through an effective memory kernel. We find that latching trajectories change the effective timescale of this kernel, a dynamical signature of transitions in the extensive-load regime. These results indicate that multi-state Potts-like representations are essential for structured memory-to-memory transitions, a hallmark of spontaneous thought.

items.title: Achiral-Chiral Dissociation and Structural Zero of the Current in the Spinterface Model of CISS
items.summary: We study the transport sector of the spinterface model of chirality-induced spin selectivity (CISS) under spin-resolved dissipation, extending the quantum non-equilibrium Green's function formulation of Ref.~\cite{Alwan2026QSpinterface} to spin-resolved lead broadenings. The spin current decomposes into an achiral part, driven by the interfacial moment, and a chiral part, driven by the Rashba spin flip. Under increasing lead spin asymmetry, the achiral part grows linearly while the chiral part follows the geometric-mean suppression, so the two sectors dissociate; they also peak at different coupling scales along the lead broadening. The coupling and bias optima are operating points of the reference configuration, not universal scaling laws. A structural zero appears at $λ_R\sin(φ/2)=t_{\mathrm{mol}}$ in the collinear-lead configuration, where the chiral signal collapses to machine precision universally across chain lengths, frequency resolutions, and twist angles; the zero originates from the rank-one singular bond matrix, whose null eigenvector traps an electron in a spin-superposition dark state that does not hop. With non-collinear ferromagnetic leads, the zero is broken in a controlled way: the residual is generically linear in the transverse polarization, arising from a single coherent spin flip at a boundary, and becomes quadratic at a tuned cancellation angle where two boundary contributions interfere destructively, with the scaling exponent jumping sharply from one to two. These results establish the spinterface model as a transport platform with a two-axis dissociation structure, non-scaling operating optima, and an exact structural zero whose non-collinear deformation is a clean linear-plus-quadratic hierarchy.

items.title: Universal model of the growth of III-V tetrahedral semiconductors on polar surfaces: pyramids and glue atoms
items.summary: Ab initio extensive calculations were used to simulate the atomic stages of the vapor growth of III-V tetrahedral semiconductors (GaN, GaP, GaAs and GaSb) from their components. The structural and electronic properties of the stoichiometric polar surfaces of III-V tetrahedral semiconductors (GaN, GaP, GaAs and GaSb), i.e. metal- and nonmetal-terminated were determined. Adsorption of the components was simulated, shown to be atomic. At low coverages adatoms occupy H3 sites, considerably stabilizing the surfaces, at high coverage, the adatoms are located in the skewed on-top positions creating the first layer necessary for growth (with the exception of nitrogen admolecules). The second adlayer is adsorbed differently: on a Ga-terminated surface it does not create pyramid structures due to strong interaction within the first NM adlayer, thus preventing effective growth. On NM terminated Ga covered surface the second NM adlayer atoms create a stable pyramid structure which is an effective vehicle for surface diffusion. Growth of III-V semiconductors occurs via the attachment of the pyramids to steps by glue atoms, i.e. additionally attached NM adatoms. The NM glue atom connection process requires additional electrons, which leads to strong dependence of the process and the entire growth on the Fermi level at the NM terminated surface

items.title: Universal model of the growth of III-V tetrahedral semiconductors on polar surfaces: pyramids and glue atoms. II. Adsorption of nonmetal atoms (N, P, As, and Sb) on Ga-terminated surfaces
items.summary: Ab initio calculations were used to simulate the adsorption processes on Ga-terminated surfaces of tetrahedral semiconductors: GaN, GaP, GaAs and GaSb. The considered adsorbates are nonmetal species, i.e., nitrogen, phosphorus, arsenic, and antimony on wurtzite gallium nitride, i.e., GaN(0001) surfaces, zinc blende gallium phosphide, i.e., GaP(111), gallium arsenide, GaAs(111), and gallium antimonide, GaSb (111) surfaces. The cases investigated include single adsorbed nonmetal atoms and full coverage, i.e. theta=1 of these surfaces. The calculated results include the stable sites and the energies of the single adsorbed atoms: located at H3 sites at low coverage and in on-top positions at high coverage for GaP, GaAs and GaSb. At high nitrogen coverage, the N2 admolecules are formed, weakly attached to the surface. The calculated electronic properties of the single-adatom systems include the band diagrams of the slabs in real and momentum space, the energies of the quantum states. In addition, the overlaps of the quantum states of the nonmetal adatoms and the nearest topmost surface Ga atoms are given. The full coverage data include the atomic configurations and the bond energies of the adsorbed layers. The electronic properties include the above-mentioned data for single adatoms, together with additional properties related to interactions between adsorbed atoms. The evaporation stability analysis confirms that the adatoms stabilize the topmost Ga atoms against detachment because of the high energy barrier of DE > 3 eV which is further increased to DE > 4 eV by coverage located at H3 sites. Thus, growth simulations should employ unreconstructed Ga-terminated surfaces covered by nonmetal atoms located at on-top positions.

items.title: Universal model of the growth of III-V tetrahedral semiconductors on polar surfaces: pyramids and glue atoms. VI. Surface diffusion on a nonmetal-terminated surface
items.summary: Ab initio calculations were used to simulate surface diffusion of adsorbates on the nonmetal-terminated surface of tetrahedral semiconductors: GaN, GaP, GaAs and GaSb. These surfaces are wurtzite gallium nitride, i.e. GaN(000-1) surface, zinc blende gallium phosphide, i.e. GaP(-1-1-1) gallium arsenide, GaAs (-1-1-1) and gallium antimonide GaSb (-1-1-1) surfaces. The mixed coverage consists of Ga adatoms in the first layer with a nonmetal atom attached above them forming a triangular-based pyramid. The pyramidal structures are stable during surface jumps involving rotations around one of the basal Ga adatoms. Thus, the diffusion proceeds via rotation (pivot) of the pair of the other basal Ga adatoms around an immobile Ga adatom moving them into new, originally empty sites. Using an energy-path determination procedure, the diffusion barriers were obtained as the difference between the initial site energy and the activated complex state energy. The detachment energy of the NM adatom was obtained assuming a final state in atomic and molecular form. The energy barrier for detachment to the atomic state is high for all atoms, on the order of 5 eV. For the molecular state these barriers are different: smaller for nitrogen, on the order of 1 eV, which is related to the high dissociation energy of the N2 molecule. For P and As the barrier is above 2 eV. For Sb it was not determined. Accordingly, the surface diffusion length is macroscopically large, indicating that all NM adatoms arrive at the steps.

items.title: Universal model of the growth of III-V tetrahedral semiconductors on polar surfaces: pyramids and glue atoms. VII. Step kinetics
items.summary: Ab initio calculations were used to simulate the kinetics of attachment of new segments of the crystalline lattice (pyramids) at steps on the nonmetal-terminated surface of tetrahedral semiconductors: GaN, GaP, GaAs and GaSb. These surfaces are wurtzite gallium nitride, i.e. GaN(000-1) surface, zinc blende gallium phosphide, i.e. GaP(-1-1-1) gallium arsenide, GaAs(-1-1-1) and gallium antimonide GaSb(-1-1-1) surfaces. Diffusion species are gallium adatoms at high coverage or gallium adatoms connected with nonmetal atom creating stable pyramids. These pyramids arrive at the steps, and cannot be attached be directly because the Ga adatom at the pyramid base cannot be attached directly. Therefore they are incorporated into the step by additional nonmetal atoms glue atoms arriving from the vapor or detached from other segments of the surface terraces.

items.title: Unconstrained $\mathbb{Z}_2$ gauge theory on a triangular lattice: deconfined fermions in a vison crystal and superfluidity
items.summary: We investigate an unconstrained $\mathbb{Z}_2$ gauge theory coupled to fermions on the triangular lattice at half filling, using auxiliary field quantum Monte Carlo simulations. The triangular geometry gives rise to a global $\mathbb{Z}_2$ symmetry that acts as an Ising symmetry on the plaquette fluxes. At weak transverse field $h$, this symmetry is spontaneously broken, stabilizing a vison crystal. We argue that this phase is deconfined: fermions, charged under an emergent $\mathbb{Z}_2$ gauge field, propagate in an ordered $π$-flux background and form a Dirac semimetal. Increasing the transverse field triggers a first-order quantum phase transition to a confined $s$-wave superfluid, at which confinement and global symmetry breaking occur simultaneously. This contrasts with the square lattice, where the corresponding transition is continuous. We extend our analysis to finite temperature and determine the thermal phase boundaries of both ordered phases. The superfluid melts through a Kosterlitz--Thouless transition, whereas the vison crystal undergoes a thermal Ising transition. Together, our results establish the $T \times h$ phase diagram and demonstrate how the triangular geometry leads to qualitative changes in both the phases and the criticality of the model.

items.title: Cup and cap synchronization: higher-order node dynamics from topology
items.summary: Higher-order node-based synchronization provides distinct mechanisms for discontinuous synchronization transitions. However, a comprehensive theoretical framework capable of encompassing existing models and revealing the role of higher-order interactions beyond triangles is still missing. Here, combining algebraic topology and nonlinear dynamics, we introduce Cup and Cap Synchronization, a unifying theoretical framework for higher-order node-based dynamics that naturally incorporates the topological organization of the underlying higher-order network. We show that Cup and Cap Synchronization can display critical behavior belonging to the universality classes of two existing higher-order Kuramoto-like models, whose distinct critical behaviors were thought to originate from different mechanisms. Remarkably, we demonstrate that Cup and Cap Synchronization displays additional phenomenology not captured by the previously proposed models of higher-order node-based synchronization. Most relevantly, the inclusion of four-body interactions can fundamentally alter the critical properties of the synchronization transition, giving rise to collective phenomena that cannot be observed in models including only interactions mediated by edges and triangles. These findings reveal the importance of going beyond the commonly studied three-body terms and establish Cup and Cap Synchronization as a unifying theoretical framework for understanding collective dynamics in higher-order networks.

items.title: Onsager Algebras and Lattice Fermions
items.summary: We study the exact Onsager algebra of free lattice fermions in staggered, Wilson, and overlap incarnations, working in both Hamiltonian and Euclidean formulations in four spacetime dimensions. In each case, we show that the exact lattice algebra emanates the full chiral symmetry of the low-energy theory: if there are $N$ massless Dirac fermions in the continuum, the Onsager algebra reduces to a $U(2N)$ chiral symmetry. The details of which generators are quantised or ultra-local differ between formulations. There is also a trade-off between the locality of generators and the maximum compact subgroup of the Onsager algebra.

items.title: Interfacial Structure and Dynamics of Active-Passive Fluid Mixtures
items.summary: We investigate the interface between an active and a passive fluid using molecular dynamics simulations of active Brownian particles in contact with a passive Lennard-Jones fluid. We compute the surface tension via two independent routes, pressure anisotropy and capillary-wave analysis, and find that they disagree systematically once activity is switched on. Static density and orientation profiles reveal three distinct activity regimes, with particles preferentially oriented toward the interface. Going beyond these static properties, we characterize the interface dynamics: a threshold activity above which mixing becomes irreversible, coinciding with the onset of the mixing regime, and a transient overshoot in interfacial width before relaxation to steady state.

items.title: Thermal conductivity of Lennard-Jones fluids from equilibrium thermodynamics
items.summary: We derive a general expression for the thermal conductivity of simple fluids within a thermodynamic transport theory (TTT) in which the Onsager coefficients of an interacting system are related to those of an ideal reference system through the ratio of the determinants of the Hessians of the relevant thermodynamic potential. The transported quantity is identified with an effective energy density proportional to the rms energy fluctuations of a small fluid cell. The result expresses the thermal conductivity as the product of its dilute-gas value and a function of equilibrium thermodynamic properties, namely the specific heats at constant density and at constant $ρT$ and the temperature derivative of the latter, with no adjustable parameters. For hard spheres, it reduces to a previously verified expression in terms of the thermodynamic factor.
